newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates firmer in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates firmer in thin trading.

text.p: Interbank rates were firmer on Friday but trading was thin as players were uncertain about the market's direction after recent volatility, dealers said.
They said rates were bidded up by smaller banks and finance companies seeking fresh funds.
"The market is still tight but there are not many players in the market. People are a bit cautious to where rates are heading," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.
"The market is much calmer this morning," he said.

Rates movements were erratic on Thursday on rumours that Bank Negara will introduce foreign exchange controls like those administered in Thailand. The talk started when the central bank called for a meeting on Friday with chief executive officers of some banks.
Banking sources, however, said Bank Negara will be meeting the bankers to discuss routine foreign exchange activities.
One-, two- and three-week money were at 8.00/20 percent against 7.5/8.0 percent on Thursday, dealers said.
One-month money was at 8.20/30 percent from 7.9/8.1, and three-month at 8.00/10 percent against 7.9/8.1.
The overnight rate, which traded between 6.5 and 9.0 percent on Thursday, was expected to move in the 7.5-8.5 percent range, traders said.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were mixed.
At 0400 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) June contract was down two basis points to 92.04, or an implied yield of 7.96 percent.
The September contract was up two at 92.43, or 7.57 percent, and December was also up two at 92.53, or 7.47 percent.
